paragraphs: In Berakhot 18b. A Babylonian, approximately of Rabbi’s generation.[^1]

notes.text: The heading explicitly makes Abba Shmuel's paternal grandfather. The opening ב is rendered In, and בבלי describes the subject as a Babylonian rather than adding Babylonian Talmud to the locator. בערך retains approximately. Full רבי remains Rabbi; its contextual reading as Yehudah HaNasi is not written in the source or independently verified here. Berakhot18b is convention-based. The relationship and approximate dating are translated as Hyman’s source claims, not admitted as new genealogical or chronological facts.
